stances.claim: A week ago, the nation was reminded once more why retired SAJ Antonio T. Carpio remains one of the most formidable defenders of Philippine sovereignty. At the turnover ceremony of the historic map '1875 Carta General del Archipiélago Filipino' to the National Library, SAJ Tony calmly but firmly urged the government to file a new arbitration case against China -- this time over the blatant denial of PH fishermen's rights at Scarborough Shoal.

For those who admire SAJ Tony's career, this latest clarion call comes as no surprise. He served with distinction on the SC for 18 years. For almost a decade, he was the Court's longest-serving SAJ -- by the way, the appellation 'SAJ' is a distinct rank granted by law to the sitting Court member serving the longest, compared to current colleagues. So respected was he that he was often called the 'Chief Justice we never had.' Time and time again, when the CJ was absent or incapacitated, SAJ Tony stepped in as acting chief, guiding the Court with 'quiet authority and unassailable integrity.'
stances.rhetorical_move: career-credential enumeration + SAJ-rank-explanation + 'Chief Justice we never had' epithet

stances.claim: Yet what he did after retirement truly elevates him to the heroic rank. Most justices, upon reaching mandatory retirement age, fade gracefully into private life. Not SAJ Tony. He made a different and far more demanding choice -- to dedicate the full weight of his remaining years to the defense of our waters. He has remained a vocal, independent figure, emphasizing the rule of law, UNCLOS, and multilateral approaches to the maritime dispute, often positioning the PH case as benefiting the international community. His postretirement work is nonpartisan and advocacy-driven rather than commercial or judicial.

During the March 23 Association of Retired Justices of the SC meeting, CJP -- as president -- paid tribute. A few years ago, during a reception for a retiring colleague, one of the 10 wealthiest Filipinos approached Carpio, and in CJP's presence, offered him a seat as independent director in his conglomerate. He politely declined: 'Thank you, but sorry I cannot accept because I want to devote my full time, energy, and resources to defending Philippine sovereignty in the West Philippine Sea.' The answer stunned the offeror -- he could hardly believe that his offer, which included substantial per diems and bonuses, would be declined.

Indeed, Carpio is the most articulate and relentless champion of the 2016 Arbitral Award -- the landmark victory affirming PH sovereignty and sovereign rights over the West Philippine Sea. He does not do it for power or popularity. He does it because he believes, as every true patriot must, that the international rule of law is the only shield of smaller nations against the world's superpowers.

Why does this matter to ordinary Filipinos? Because fishing rights are not abstract legal concepts. They are the daily bread of thousands of fishermen whose livelihoods depend on rich waters. When they are blocked, it is not merely a diplomatic tiff -- it is an assault on their right to feed their families. It is about liberty -- freedom to navigate territorial waters without fear and harassment. It is about overflight -- right of PH aircraft to fly over waters indisputably ours. And it is about prosperity -- sovereign right to explore and develop oil, gas, and other resources within the exclusive economic zone, including the promising Reed Bank, which SAJ Tony has repeatedly bemoaned has remained untapped due to outside forces. These are the foundations of national dignity and economic survival.
stances.rhetorical_move: ordinary-Filipino-fishing-rights-as-daily-bread + liberty + overflight + prosperity (Reed Bank-untapped) tripartite framework

stances.claim: In an era when some would rather take the opposite view, SAJ Tony stands as a beacon of principled resistance. He reminds us that true friendship among nations is built on mutual respect for the law, not on the surrender of sovereign rights. The government may not have acted yet on his recommendation for a new case. But history will record that when others wavered, one man -- retired from active government service -- never stopped fighting with the same intellectual rigor and patriotic fire that defined his judicial career.

Some may oppose his assertions -- that is their right in our democracy. In a similar way, though CJP praises him for his relentlessness and patriotism, CJP did not always agree with him. When both were incumbents, they clashed on Carpio's advocacy for the death penalty, while CJP fearlessly opposed it as violative of the Constitution and God's commands. Carpio shows strength not through force, but through the calm and principled exercise of due process, grounded in respect for the rule of law and international covenants. Critics may disagree, but CJP thinks Carpio's wisdom and unwavering research are more than enough to prevail in any international tribunal. SAJ Tony had left the bench, but he has never left the battlefield for the country. For that, our people owe him a debt of gratitude. He remains, in CJP's humble opinion, a relentless defender of Philippine sovereignty -- a modern-day hero.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes a tribute-column for retired Senior Associate Justice Antonio T. Carpio, 'one of the most formidable defenders of Philippine sovereignty.' A week ago, at the turnover ceremony of the historic '1875 Carta General del Archipiélago Filipino' map to the National Library, SAJ Tony calmly but firmly urged the government to file a new arbitration case against China -- this time over the blatant denial of PH fishermen's rights at Scarborough Shoal. The clarion call surprises no one familiar with his career. He served with distinction on the SC for 18 years; for almost a decade he was the longest-serving SAJ (a distinct law-granted rank for the sitting Court member serving longest among current colleagues). So respected was he that he was often called the 'Chief Justice we never had' -- time and again, when the CJ was absent or incapacitated, SAJ Tony stepped in as acting chief, guiding the Court with 'quiet authority and unassailable integrity.' Yet it is what he did after retirement that truly elevates him to the heroic rank. Most justices fade gracefully into private life upon mandatory retirement -- not SAJ Tony. He made a different and far more demanding choice: to dedicate the full weight of his remaining years to the defense of our waters. He has remained a vocal, independent figure, emphasizing the rule of law, UNCLOS, and multilateral approaches to the maritime dispute, often positioning the PH case as benefiting the international community. His postretirement work is nonpartisan and advocacy-driven rather than commercial or judicial. During the March 23 2026 Association of Retired Justices of the SC meeting, CJP -- as president -- paid tribute. A few years ago, during a reception for a retiring colleague, one of the 10 wealthiest Filipinos approached Carpio in CJP's presence and offered him a seat as independent director in his conglomerate. He politely declined: 'Thank you, but sorry I cannot accept because I want to devote my full time, energy, and resources to defending Philippine sovereignty in the West Philippine Sea.' The answer stunned the offeror, who could hardly believe his offer -- which included substantial per diems and bonuses -- would be declined. Carpio is the most articulate and relentless champion of the 2016 Arbitral Award -- the landmark victory affirming PH sovereignty and sovereign rights over the West Philippine Sea. He does not do it for power or popularity. He does it because he believes, as every true patriot must, that the international rule of law is the only shield of smaller nations against the world's superpowers. Why does this matter to ordinary Filipinos? Because fishing rights are not abstract legal concepts -- they are the daily bread of thousands of fishermen whose livelihoods depend on rich waters. When blocked, it is not merely a diplomatic tiff but an assault on their right to feed their families. It is about liberty -- freedom to navigate territorial waters without fear and harassment. It is about overflight -- the right of PH aircraft to fly over waters indisputably ours. And it is about prosperity -- the sovereign right to explore and develop oil, gas, and other resources within the exclusive economic zone, including the promising Reed Bank, which SAJ Tony has repeatedly bemoaned has remained untapped due to outside forces. These are the foundations of national dignity and economic survival. In an era when some would rather take the opposite view, SAJ Tony stands as a beacon of principled resistance, reminding us that true friendship among nations is built on mutual respect for the law, not on the surrender of sovereign rights. The government may not have acted yet on his recommendation for a new case. But history will record that when others wavered, one man -- retired from active government service -- never stopped fighting with the same intellectual rigor and patriotic fire that defined his judicial career. Some may oppose his assertions -- that is their right in our democracy. In a similar way, though CJP praises him for his relentlessness and patriotism, CJP did not always agree with him: when both were incumbents, they clashed on his advocacy for the death penalty, while CJP fearlessly opposed it as violative of the Constitution and God's commands. He shows strength not through force, but through the calm and principled exercise of due process, grounded in respect for the rule of law and international covenants. Critics may disagree with him, but his wisdom and unwavering research are more than enough to prevail in any international tribunal. SAJ Tony had left the bench, but he has never left the battlefield for the country. For that, our people owe him a debt of gratitude. He remains a relentless defender of Philippine sovereignty -- a modern-day hero.
